messages:
jonathan: ran a quick host-side profile on canary, tail latency up ~12% for small (<=64 token) responses. digging into preproc+ingress.

maya: interesting — we rolled the kernel-selector tweak last night. did you see any kernel mismatch logs?

jonathan: not obvious in runtime logs, but strace-ish flame shows lots of short syscalls from tokenizer: read()/writev() in tight loops. grpc frames are tiny.

liam: that matches what i saw on proxy machines — http2 WINDOW_UPDATE fragmentation causing many 1-2KB frames, grpc layer then does small writes. adds syscall overhead on host.

sophie: kv-cache metrics from the same window: hot_shard_misses spiked x3, eviction_rate doubled. likely causes smaller batches because batching heuristic sees lower effective reuse.

jonathan: so hypothesis: kernel-selector changed kernel choice at short sequence lengths -> different memory/KV access pattern -> more kv misses -> autoadjust batching reduces batch size -> more small writes and tokenization syscall churn -> host latency tail.

maya: can we validate by forcing old kernel choice on canary and re-run profile? if latency falls, we have a direct causal link.

liam: also want to test coalescing at the ingress layer. short-term mitigations: increase http2 write coalesce window, and add a small writev coalescer in proxy.

jonathan: repro commands i used:
```bash
# run 1m steady qps at 60rps, short prompts
wrk -t4 -c50 -d60s --script=short_prompt.lua https://canary-ingress.redwood/api/v1/generate
# host profiler snapshot
python tools/host_profiler.py --target proxy-1 --duration 60 --out /tmp/profile.json
```

sophie: i pushed KV cache debug traces to the perf bucket: gs://perf-debug/1748001111/kv-traces.tar.gz

devex-bot: linked perf dashboard -> <https://perf.redwood.dev/dashboards/ingress-host-overhead?run=1748001111>

jonathan: next steps: (1) toggle kernel-selector to previous commit on canary, (2) enable proxy write coalescer, (3) re-run steady-state profile and compare kv-miss/batch-size/syscall counts. i'll take (1) & (3). maya/liam can do (2).

maya: ack, i'll prepare the rollback patch and schedule a quick canary.

liam: i'll prototype a lightweight writev coalescer in proxy; should be a one-file change. posting WIP in ~30m. :hammer_and_wrench:

sophie: i'll keep watching kv metrics and feed results back. if eviction pattern persists we may need to tweak kv-sharding or prefetch hints.

runtime-bot: perf job queued -> job_id=perf-1748001111-1; notify @eng-runtime when complete.

jonathan: thanks all — aim to have results within 3 hours. if anyone sees anything surprising ping here or drop traces in the perf bucket. :mag_right:
